item.text:
**1B.1 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: I found strong evidence that Putin’s 2024 behavior mostly **increased** nuclear/existential risk or at least normalized it as a coercive tool. I found only weak counterevidence: Putin occasionally framed nuclear moves as “deterrence” or “exercise,” but I did not find a concrete 2024 action that clearly reduced nuclear risk in the arms-control sense.

### Accepted claims

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Against 1B.1 | `Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence` | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598 | Putin signed a new nuclear deterrence doctrine replacing the 2020 version. The text says it identifies threats to be neutralized by nuclear deterrence and specifies conditions for nuclear use. That is evidence of formalizing and potentially widening escalation space, not reducing existential risk. | 1B.1 |
| Against 1B.1 | `Russia says it will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Reuters reported the doctrine change as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. That frames the move as coercive escalation tied to wartime leverage, not risk reduction. | 1B.1 |
| Against 1B.1 | `Answers by Vladimir Putin and Alexander Lukashenko to media questions` | President of Russia | 2024-05-09 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002 | Putin said a tactical nuclear-weapons drill was “not about using these weapons” and “just routine work.” This is the strongest restraint-flavored evidence I found, but it is only rhetoric about an exercise, not a step that actually lowers nuclear risk. | 1B.1 |
| Against 1B.1 | `Report: Russian army meeting / updated deterrence principles` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/75887 | Putin said Russia had “specified” the principles for using nuclear weapons and kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert with continued exercises. He also linked this to response against U.S. missile deployments. This supports an escalatory posture. | 1B.1 |
| Against 1B.1 | `Russia will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Same source also shows the justification was external pressure in the Ukraine war, not arms control or de-escalation. I’m keeping it because it directly informs the escalation-vs-restraint balance. | 1B.1 |
| Weakly for 1B.1 | `Answers by Vladimir Putin and Alexander Lukashenko to media questions` | President of Russia | 2024-05-09 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002 | The “this is not about using these weapons” line is the closest thing to de-escalatory rhetoric I found in 2024. It is limited, because the surrounding context was a live tactical nuclear exercise involving Belarus. | 1B.1 |

### Synthesis

- **Best-supported reading:** Putin did **not** seek to reduce nuclear or existential risk in 2024; he instead **normalized deterrence brinkmanship**.
- **Why:** the key 2024 Kremlin action was an updated nuclear doctrine, followed by rhetoric about constant readiness, exercises, and response to Western threats.
- **Counterevidence:** Putin’s May 9 remark that the tactical nuclear drill was “not about using these weapons” is a restraint signal, but it is too thin to outweigh the doctrine update and readiness posture.
- **Search gap:** I did **not** find a credible 2024 Putin action showing genuine nuclear-risk reduction such as arms-control revival, de-alerting, test restraint, or a new non-use commitment. The available evidence points mostly in the opposite direction.
